title: Add closed ticket status and close-ticket command
story: As a developer, I want to close a ticket without completing programming work, so that I can track intentional decisions to skip or abandon a ticket.
acceptance_criteria: A 'closed' status is a valid terminal status alongside 'done'
A close-ticket.py script exists in scripts/ that sets a ticket's status to 'closed' and prompts for an optional reason via stdin
The optional reason is stored in the ticket JSON
Closed tickets are treated as terminal — they are not pulled into future sprints
sprint-close and retro do not break when closed tickets are present
agent_retro: The ticket named the new script close-ticket.py but that name was already taken by the done-setting script — required a clarifying question before starting. The ticket story should have made the rename explicit.

title: Snapshot tests for all Storybook stories
story: As a developer, I want automatic snapshot tests for every Storybook story so that I can refactor code without worrying that I've changed what actually gets rendered.
acceptance_criteria: Every existing Storybook story has a corresponding snapshot test
Every new Storybook story must have a corresponding snapshot test
Snapshot tests capture the rendered DOM tree
Failing snapshot tests block the build
Developers can regenerate snapshots using an existing command when rendering changes are intentional
agent_retro: The initial approach (direct render via RTL) differed from the Storybook-recommended portable stories pattern. User redirected to the storyshots migration guide mid-implementation, which required switching to composeStories + story.run() + setProjectAnnotations. Could have discovered this upfront by reading the docs before proposing.
user_retro: Though tests pass, the new storyshot tests surfaced an error message related to typing.

title: Validate API key on exercise start
story: As a user, I want my API key validated when I press Start Exercise so that I don't waste time completing an exercise only to discover the key is invalid.
acceptance_criteria: When Start is pressed, the API key is validated before the exercise begins
While validation is in flight, the Start button is disabled and shows a loading indicator
If validation succeeds, the exercise starts normally
If validation fails, an inline error message is shown near the API key field and the exercise does not start
The error message is specific to the failure type (invalid/revoked key, network error, etc.)
agent_retro: The validateApiKey tests in analysisService.test.ts instantiate Anthropic error classes with full SDK constructor signatures (status, error, message, headers) even though the mock classes are plain `class X extends Error {}` that silently ignore those args. This works at runtime but creates a hidden coupling — if the mock class ever added a real constructor, the extra args would start mattering. The test pattern could instead just use `new Error()` with a name property or a simpler mock approach.
user_retro: i'd like there to be a step in doing a ticket where the agent asks the user if it's time to be done with the ticket and add retro comments.

title: New story stub script
story: As a developer, I want a script that creates a stub story ticket so that I can quickly capture an idea without going through the full grooming process.
acceptance_criteria: Script accepts a title/one-liner as a command-line argument
Script appends a new ticket to the backlog with the provided title and empty fields matching the existing ticket JSON format
Script uses next-ticket-id.py to determine and increment the ticket ID
Script exits with code 0 on success and nonzero on error

title: as a developer, i want to ensure that as stories are groomed according to my conventions
acceptance_criteria: when stories are groomed, implementation details are left out of acceptance criteria
when stories are groomed, the agent looks for gaps or conflicts or vague direction and collaborates with the user to improve acceptance criteria.
grooming is extracted into its own skill
